status_summary: HRSA's FY 2026 General Terms and Conditions, applying to awards made on or after 2026-03-11, add a section requiring funded activities to align with HRSA priorities, including not supporting medical interventions for gender dysphoria in minors that lack a strong evidence base and applying sex-based definitions grounded in biology. According to the government's court filing, Ryan White funding notices first published 2026-06-04 limit sex hormones dispensed through AIDS Drug Assistance Programs to HIV-related uses and bar funds for denying the sex binary. Provider groups challenged both in the District of Massachusetts on 2026-06-10 (No. 26-cv-12638); after a trial, the government filed a post-hearing brief on 2026-10-09 and no ruling was found. No source read states that earlier HRSA guidance on gender transition services was formally withdrawn.

title: Withdraw HRSA Ryan White guidance allowing funds for gender transition support
uncertainties: In review the HRSA FY 2026 General Terms and Conditions were read on hrsa.gov: they apply to awards on or after 2026-03-11, contain the priorities on gender dysphoria interventions for minors and sex-based definitions, do not name the Ryan White program, and state that terms enjoined by a court do not apply to covered recipients. The Ryan White funding notice terms were read only as described in the government's June 2026 brief; the notices themselves were not opened. The government gives 2026-06-04 for the first notice and plaintiffs' counsel gives 2026-06-08. Consolidation (2026-07-20) and the trial date (2026-09-23) come from plaintiffs' counsel's case page and are not separate timeline events; the 2026-10-09 government post-hearing brief confirms a trial was held and no ruling had issued. Neither government brief mentions withdrawal of earlier HRSA guidance on gender transition services, and that withdrawal remains unverified. The match is partial because the recommendation asks for withdrawal of guidance while the action restricts funding through award terms.
